before: Intratumoral means within a tumour; intralesional means within a lesion. Intratumoral immunotherapy combines a route with an immune-directed treatment purpose. The name does not identify the substance, and a locally injected cytotoxic drug need not be immunotherapy. An in-situ vaccination strategy seeks useful immune learning from material in the body; it is not a synonym for every injection. Local-material and learning analogies leave direct drug effects and procedure risks unresolved.

A lesion-based injection needs an identified site that can be reached safely by the specified method. The accessible lesion may not represent every other tumour site. Entry of a needle does not establish uniform distribution, confined exposure or systemic safety. Recruitment or activation of presenting cells, antigen collection and priming can be investigated, while travel to another lesion, natural recognition and sustained function remain separate questions. Inflammation, local injury, infection and systemic effects depend on the product and procedure.

Hammerich's 2019 report studied a particular strategy in indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Flt3 ligand, low-dose radiation and the TLR3 agonist poly-ICLC. NCT01976585 specifies intratumoral Flt3 ligand and poly-ICLC with low-dose radiotherapy. It does not make every injected immune agent the same intervention. Marabelle's 2018 paper is an expert terminology and reporting recommendation, rather than a trial establishing efficacy of the class.

Keep three measurements separate. Changes in size or tissue at the injected lesion show local observations. Controlled assays of antigen-reactive cells ask an immune-response question but leave natural recognition and function elsewhere unresolved. Changes at uninjected lesions ask another question, while the injection's added effect and longer-term patient benefit need a suitable comparison. Report each component's route and serial injected and uninjected lesion results. An uninjected lesion can still receive systemic co-treatment, so it need not be untreated.

The U.S. Imlygic label specifies talimogene laherparepvec for local treatment of unresectable cutaneous, subcutaneous and nodal melanoma lesions recurrent after initial surgery. It states that improved overall survival and an effect on visceral metastases have not been shown. A local melanoma indication does not establish whole-body benefit or a breast-cancer indication. Intralesional administration also does not remove the label's infection, wound and other product-specific precautions.

before: First define the irradiated field and the actual exposure of each lesion. A local response does not demonstrate a distant response. Demaria’s bilateral 67NR mammary-tumour mouse experiment combined local radiation with Flt3 ligand. The distant tumour grew more slowly under the combination, whereas radiation alone affected the irradiated tumour; antigen-mismatched and T-cell-deficient comparisons supported an immune-dependent component. This is a defined combined animal intervention, not a human response rate. Postow’s ipilimumab-plus-radiation melanoma report was one case with temporal immune correlates, not a study of frequency.

Formenti enrolled 39 people with chemotherapy-refractory metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer in a single-arm radiation-plus-ipilimumab study. At day 88, 21 had completed treatment and response assessment. Seven responses were 7/39, about 18% of those enrolled, or 7/21, about 33% of those evaluable. Seventeen received fewer than four cycles because they progressed or died before day 88; another completed four cycles without response assessment. These denominators answer different questions and neither estimates radiation-alone activity or an individual breast-cancer response probability.

To assess a distant effect, retain lesion exposure, serial imaging, prespecified response rules, timing and concurrent therapies. There is no universal abscopal cutoff or percentage across cancers and regimens; case observations, model mechanisms and comparative clinical outcomes are different evidence tiers.

before: BOOSTER studied ablation during ongoing immunotherapy after limited residual lung disease; CURB studied SBRT for oligoprogression in lung and breast cohorts; NRG-BR002 studied ablation during first-line systemic treatment for limited metastatic breast cancer. after: BOOSTER studied ablation during ongoing immunotherapy after limited residual lung disease; CURB studied SBRT for oligoprogression in lung and breast cohorts; NRG-BR002 studied ablation during first-line systemic treatment for limited metastatic breast cancer. PACIFIC tested consolidation durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy in nonprogressing stage III lung cancer. These are distinct settings and intervention contrasts.

Start with the goal and history before choosing a clock. A smaller lesion is a response observation at assessment; local control concerns keeping that site from progressing during follow-up. Postoperative local-recurrence prevention, relief of pain from a bone metastasis and a growing lesion during otherwise controlled metastatic disease are different questions. A meaningful pain improvement need not wait for an untreated tumour to shrink. A positive blood molecular test does not identify a lesion's position, boundary or safe access. An earlier scan date alone does not demonstrate improved outcomes. These distinctions organise evidence review rather than select a dose, procedure or treatment date. Nonmetastatic disease means no established distant metastases; a stage and subtype still need their own comparison of local and systemic care. Recovery, healing, previous exposure, overlapping toxicities and protocol assessment times supply other clocks. They are reasons to examine the studied sequence rather than invent a universal interval or repeat a procedure whenever a blood marker rises.

A local-treatment proposal needs five connected answers: the local and hoped-for wider outcomes with their measurements; evidence matching the cancer, disease history, complete strategy and comparator; access, intended coverage, margins, motion and nearby structures; actual exposure and normal-tissue risk; and alternatives, burdens and remaining uncertainty. In a fictional pair of equally sized lesions, proximity to a sensitive airway and a different approach can change feasibility. Depth alone is also insufficient: some deep lesions can be accessed, while a superficial lesion can have a difficult margin. Small diameter and a positive tracer scan settle none of the wider immune or outcome claims. Comparators can include systemic treatment alone, another local strategy, observation where appropriate or a study; include visits, recovery and additional sampling among the burdens. For a tracer and therapeutic product, establish the relationship between them rather than treating target uptake as a measured therapeutic dose. This review identifies missing facts and does not authorise treatment.

Delivery can be compared without ranking treatments. A fictional probe card controls a selected liver site, a beam card specifies a lung volume and motion assessment, and a radioactive-drug card requires distribution, retention and organ dosimetry. They are different routes, not a ladder from one lesion to invisible disease. A systemically distributed radioactive product still does not guarantee exposure of every microscopic deposit. Radiation injury does not require a conventional T cell to recognise peptide-HLA; proposed antigen-specific immune effects still need presentation, access, recognition and function. In another invented study, people receiving the same systemic strategy are randomised to a local addition or no local addition. With the same defined progression endpoint, starting time and follow-up, treated sites are controlled but new lesions occur in both arms and the progression-free-survival interval spans effects in both directions. That supports local control while leaving the added progression effect uncertain; survival, quality of life, pain and harms remain separate outcomes.

PACIFIC's five-year report concerns durvalumab versus placebo after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation in unresectable, nonprogressing stage III non-small-cell lung cancer. The report found sustained progression-free and overall-survival benefit for that tested consolidation strategy. It did not require stereotactic body radiation, identify an abscopal mechanism or establish that focused radiation should always precede checkpoint treatment across cancers. Randomised comparisons, development phase and publication format answer different questions; these study cards cannot rank technologies from separate headlines. A case can describe a clinical course, a nonrandomised comparison can be distorted by treatment selection, and a model can supply a rationale for testing. These designs do not establish the same causal claim.

summary.before: Oligoprogression describes the situation in which only one or two lesions grow while the rest of the cancer remains controlled on a targeted therapy. In ALK- and EGFR-driven non-small-cell lung cancer the usual response is local ablative treatment of the progressing lesions, with stereotactic radiotherapy or surgery, while the tyrosine kinase inhibitor continues, which extends the time a patient stays on an effective systemic therapy. It is distinct from oligometastatic disease at diagnosis, where the whole burden is limited from the start. The concept is linked from the bottlenecks on tumour heterogeneity and on metastasis biology, from the resistance-routes map, and from the idea of a test to tell true oligometastatic disease from hidden widespread spread.
summary.after:
Oligoprogression describes limited progression within otherwise controlled metastatic disease during treatment. It is not restricted to one or two lesions or to targeted pills: the number, imaging rules and prior treatment depend on the definition being used. Oligometastatic disease describes limited detected distant spread, while limited residual disease describes what remains after treatment; retain the earlier burden and whether the remaining lesions are growing.

Treating progressing sites while continuing systemic therapy is a strategy to evaluate, rather than an automatic instruction. CURB tested adding stereotactic body radiation to standard care in lung and breast cohorts with different results. A current lesion count cannot establish benefit, safety or which systemic treatment should continue.

after: CURB was an open-label randomised phase 2 study after at least first-line systemic treatment, defining oligoprogression as at most five progressive lesions on CT or PET-CT. The prespecified lung cohort had median progression-free survival of 10.0 months with SBRT plus standard care versus 2.2 with standard care, hazard ratio 0.41, 95% confidence interval 0.22 to 0.75. The breast cohort had 4.4 versus 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.78, interval 0.43 to 1.43. Failure to show a breast-cohort improvement does not establish an exact zero effect or a precise effect in every breast subtype. The intervention, comparator and harms must stay with the population.

In two fictional current scan reports, each maps two lesions. Card A previously had eight before checkpoint treatment and now has two nongrowing residual lesions; card B had two during systemic treatment and now has one growing while the other remains controlled. A poses a limited-residual-disease question and B a limited-progression question. Equal current counts do not make the histories interchangeable or establish trial eligibility, an optimal procedure or a timing rule. BOOSTER studied a response-selected residual lung-cancer setting; CURB selected progression after systemic treatment.

before: A few lit windows show what is detectable, not a census of every room. This analogy does not mean that every limited pattern conceals widespread disease. Synchronous metastases are detected near the initial diagnosis; metachronous metastases are detected later, with the interval defined by the author or protocol. Induced limited disease follows previously widespread disease and systemic treatment. Oligoprogression means a growing subset while other disease remains controlled during treatment. Limited residual or persistent disease means limited visible disease remains after treatment; specify whether it is stable or progressing. These labels are not universal synonyms.

The SABR-COMET randomised phase 2 study enrolled 99 selected patients with different primary cancers, including 18 with breast cancer, a controlled primary and one to five treatable metastases. Its extended follow-up found eight-year overall survival of 27.2% with SABR plus standard care versus 13.6% with standard care alone, with grade 2 or higher acute or late toxicity of 30.3% versus 9.1%. This mixed-cancer result is not a definitive TNBC treatment effect. Control of an irradiated site, delay in progression, survival and symptom relief are different outcomes.

NRG-BR002 tested adding ablation to first-line systemic therapy in breast cancer with at most four metastases, controlled primary disease, at most 12 months of first-line therapy without progression, and all visible sites amenable to SBRT or resection. Of 129 enrolled patients, 125 were eligible for analysis and 79% had HR-positive/HER2-negative disease. Median progression-free survival was 23.0 months without ablation and 19.5 months with it; the hazard ratio was 0.92, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.57 to 1.47. Overall survival did not differ significantly and the study did not proceed to phase 3. This does not supply a definitive effect for every subtype or erase a separate symptom-relief goal.

Classification uses the imaging and its coverage and sensitivity, lesion and organ counts, locations, sizes, dates, previous burden, systemic treatment and response or progression history. A biopsy may be needed to confirm a finding, but classification is not inherently a tumour-consuming molecular assay. Benign mimics, undetected lesions and missing earlier records can mislead. Keep a protocol's count, timing, primary-control and treatability requirements; five lesions is not a cure cutoff and a molecular result does not universally establish this state.

Vanpouille-Box's 2017 experiments found that sufficiently high single radiation doses induced the DNA-degrading enzyme TREX1, reducing cytosolic DNA and interferon signalling. The threshold sufficient to clear cytosolic DNA varied from twelve to eighteen gray across the tested mouse and human carcinoma cell lines; a patient-derived lung-cancer xenograft was also examined. The work connected repeated lower-dose irradiation, type I interferon and dendritic-cell-dependent T-cell effects in defined models with checkpoint blockade. It does not supply a universal human dose ceiling, show that more physical injury always gives more useful immunity or select an individual radiation schedule.

summary.before: Cytosolic double-stranded DNA (from micronuclei after DNA damage, or from dying tumour cells taken up by dendritic cells) is sensed by cGAS, producing cGAMP, which activates STING on the ER, recruiting TBK1 to phosphorylate IRF3 and NF-κB, driving type I interferon and chemokines (CXCL10) that recruit and prime T cells. Explains the immunogenic effects of radiation (abscopal effect), PARP inhibitors, and TOP1-payload ADCs. Tumours silence STING or express ENPP1 (degrades cGAMP). STING agonists as drugs have disappointed; ENPP1 inhibitors and STING-agonist ADCs are being tested. Sensor and messenger are separate steps: in cell experiments cGAS bound DNA in the cytoplasm and made the second messenger cGAMP, which binds and activates STING (Sun et al., 2013), and the presence of DNA does not by itself measure cGAS activity. summary.before: The tumour microenvironment, as Wikipedia describes it, is the ecosystem of cancer cells, stromal tissue, immune cells and extracellular matrix around a tumour. Any measurement on the whole sample (bulk expression, methylation, a region of a spatial section) averages over that mix, so an apparent risk or subtype difference between regions or patients can be a composition difference rather than a change in the cancer cells themselves. Deconvolution and purity estimates are the usual corrections.
summary.after:
A tumour specimen can contain malignant, immune, stromal and normal cells. A difference in an aggregate molecular signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells or both. That is different from a directly counted cell fraction or a density per sampled area, each of which also needs its denominator and sampled region.

Preparation can change what is recovered. Slyper and colleagues compared single-cell and single-nucleus profiling in matched tumour specimens and found similar cell types at sometimes different proportions. tldr.before: A way of converting any radiotherapy schedule into a common currency so that, say, five big doses can be compared with 25 small ones. EQD2 expresses the same thing as the equivalent total dose in 2 Gy fractions.
tldr.after: Biologically effective dose compares radiation patterns under a stated model and tissue assumption. It does not establish equal clinical outcomes or safety.

summary.before: Because the effect of radiation depends on fraction size as well as total dose, physicists calculate the biologically effective dose from the total dose, the dose per fraction and the tissue's alpha/beta ratio. EQD2 rescales this to the dose that would have the same effect if given in 2 Gy fractions, the historical standard. Both are used to design hypofractionated schedules, sum doses in re-irradiation and compare brachytherapy with external beam.
summary.after:
Biologically effective dose, or BED, is calculated from a radiation pattern and a specified tissue-and-endpoint model. In the basic equal-fraction linear-quadratic calculation, both total dose and dose per fraction matter, together with the assumed alpha/beta ratio. The result is a modelled quantity reported in gray, not extra physical dose.

EQD2 expresses the dose in two-gray fractions that would give the same modelled effect under the same assumptions. Neither expression is a universal conversion between any schedules. Repair, time, distribution and model validity must be considered for the actual irradiation pattern; numerical equivalence does not establish equivalent control or harm.

after: For equal brief external-beam fractions, the basic linear-quadratic expression is BED = n × d × [1 + d/(alpha/beta)]. Here n is the count, d is dose per fraction in gray and alpha/beta is a tissue-and-endpoint parameter in gray, so the ratio inside the bracket is dimensionless. The simplified expression assumes negligible repair during delivery and complete repair between fractions, and omits overall time and repopulation. Prolonged or internally distributed irradiation needs additional modelling; this expression does not automatically compare every brachytherapy or radioligand pattern.

Two invented patterns, fifteen fractions of two gray and five of six gray, each total thirty gray. At an assumed alpha/beta of three gray, their BED values are fifty and ninety gray; at an assumed ten gray, they are 36 and 48. The between-pattern difference is forty under the first assumption and twelve under the second. These assumed parameters are not measurements of a person's cancer or organs. Lower alpha/beta gives fraction size more weight at fixed total dose; a low-ratio tumour narrows a contrast inferred using a ten-gray tumour assumption.

Higher calculated BED means a larger modelled effect under the stated column's assumptions, rather than an observed benefit or toxicity probability. Dose distribution, exposed volume, intervals, overall duration, other exposures, population, comparator, endpoint and follow-up remain necessary. Arithmetic cannot validate extrapolation to a fraction size or settle parameter uncertainty. Five sessions do not identify stereotactic delivery, and this equation measures neither priming nor an abscopal response or immune threshold.

tldr.before: The equation radiotherapy uses to compare schedules: cell kill has a part proportional to dose and a part proportional to dose squared, and the ratio between them (alpha over beta) tells you how much a tissue cares about the size of each fraction.
tldr.after: A model of radiation response combines a term proportional to dose with one proportional to dose squared. Its use depends on the tissue, endpoint and irradiation pattern.

summary.before: The linear-quadratic model describes the surviving fraction of cells after a dose d as exp(minus alpha d minus beta d squared). Tissues and tumours with a high alpha/beta ratio (around 10 Gy, most tumours and acutely reacting tissues) are little affected by fraction size; those with a low ratio (around 3 Gy for late-reacting normal tissue, and perhaps 1.5 Gy for prostate cancer) are very sensitive to it. Jack Fowler and others turned this into the biologically effective dose, which lets clinicians compare a 25-fraction course with a five-fraction one and underpins hypofractionation, stereotactic dosing and re-irradiation sums. The model breaks down at very large fractions and ignores repopulation unless extended. Relative biological effectiveness rescales the gray before the linear-quadratic formula is applied; a proton plan at RBE 1.1 and the same plan at a variable, LET-weighted RBE are different EQD2 maps.
summary.after:
The linear-quadratic model expresses the surviving cell fraction after dose d as exp(-alpha × d - beta × d squared). The alpha/beta ratio is a parameter in gray for a specified tissue and endpoint. At fixed total physical dose, a lower ratio gives fraction size greater weight. Historical teaching values near ten gray for many tumours and early-responding tissues such as skin and mucosa, and three for late normal-tissue effects, are conventions rather than constants for every tumour or organ. The trialists interpreted these estimates as similar fraction-size sensitivity for breast cancer and its dose-limiting normal tissues.

The basic equal-fraction calculation assumes equal effects per fraction and complete repair between fractions and does not include overall treatment time. Too short an interval or slow repair can violate that assumption. Extrapolation to a large fraction size or prolonged irradiation needs assessment; a model calculation alone validates neither the pattern nor clinical equivalence.

Relative biological effectiveness rescales the gray before the linear-quadratic formula is applied; a proton plan at RBE 1.1 and the same plan at a variable, LET-weighted RBE are different EQD2 maps.

after.summary: Paired-specimen studies found that fixation and extraction changed nucleic-acid measurements relative to fresh-frozen material. No preparation is universally best; the intended measurement and evidence for that particular workflow determine suitability.

rows.before: cGAS-STING هو جهاز الإنذار في الخلية لوجود DNA في المكان الخطأ. يتسبب الإشعاع والعلاج الكيميائي وأدوية ADC في تسرّب DNA إلى السيتوبلازم؛ فيكتشفه cGAS، ويُطلق STING الإنذار، ويستدعي الإنترفيرون الجهاز المناعي.
rows.after: cGAS هو مستشعر للحمض النووي DNA يمكنه تنشيط الإشارات عبر STING. تعتمد الإشارة المقاسة والنتيجة المناعية على الخلية والسياق.

rows.before: عندما تنمو بقعة واحدة أو بقعتان فقط في ظل علاج موجّه فعّال في ما عدا ذلك؛ تُعالج البقع ويُستمر في القرص.
rows.after: التقدم محدود البؤر يعني أن عدداً محدوداً من الآفات يتقدم بينما يبقى المرض في المواضع الأخرى تحت السيطرة أثناء العلاج. ويعتمد تعريفه والدليل على إضافة علاج موضعي على الحالة السريرية أو تصميم الدراسة.

rows.before: cGAS-STING ist der Alarm der Zelle für DNA am falschen Ort. Strahlung, Chemotherapie und ADCs lassen DNA ins Zytoplasma gelangen; cGAS erkennt sie, STING schlägt Alarm, und Interferon ruft das Immunsystem herbei.
rows.after: cGAS ist ein DNA-Sensor, der die Signalübertragung über STING aktivieren kann. Das gemessene Signal und die Immunwirkung hängen von der Zelle und dem Kontext ab.

rows.before: Wenn unter einer ansonsten wirksamen zielgerichteten Therapie nur ein oder zwei Herde wachsen; die Herde behandeln und die Tablette beibehalten.
rows.after: Bei einer Oligoprogression schreitet eine begrenzte Zahl von Herden fort, während die übrige Erkrankung unter der Behandlung kontrolliert bleibt. Definition und Evidenz für eine zusätzliche lokale Behandlung hängen vom klinischen Kontext oder der Studie ab.

rows.before: Cuando solo crecen uno o dos focos mientras una terapia dirigida sigue funcionando; se tratan los focos y se mantiene la pastilla.
rows.after: En la oligoprogresión avanza un conjunto limitado de lesiones mientras el resto de la enfermedad sigue controlado durante el tratamiento. La definición y la evidencia para añadir tratamiento local dependen del contexto clínico o del estudio.

rows.before: La alarma de la célula ante ADN fuera de lugar. La radiación, la quimioterapia y los ADC derraman ADN en el citoplasma; cGAS lo detecta, STING da la alarma y el interferón llama al sistema inmunitario.
rows.after: cGAS es un sensor de ADN que puede activar la señalización a través de STING. La señal medida y el efecto inmunitario dependen de la célula y del contexto.

rows.before: cGAS-STING est l'alarme de la cellule face à du DNA qui se trouve au mauvais endroit. La radiothérapie, la chimiothérapie et les ADC répandent du DNA dans le cytoplasme ; cGAS le détecte, STING déclenche l'alarme et l'interféron appelle le système immunitaire.
rows.after: cGAS est un capteur d’ADN qui peut activer la signalisation par STING. Le signal mesuré et l’effet immunitaire dépendent de la cellule et du contexte.

rows.before: Lorsque seulement un ou deux foyers progressent sous une thérapie ciblée par ailleurs efficace ; on traite les foyers et on garde le comprimé.
rows.after: L’oligoprogression désigne la progression d’un nombre limité de lésions alors que le reste de la maladie demeure contrôlé pendant le traitement. Sa définition et les données sur l’ajout d’un traitement local dépendent du contexte clinique ou de l’étude.

rows.before: जब अन्यथा काम कर रही लक्षित चिकित्सा पर केवल एक-दो स्थान बढ़ें; स्थानों का इलाज करें और गोली जारी रखें।
rows.after: ओलिगोप्रोग्रेशन में उपचार के दौरान कुछ सीमित घाव बढ़ते हैं, जबकि बाकी कैंसर नियंत्रण में रहता है। इसकी परिभाषा और स्थानीय उपचार जोड़ने के प्रमाण रोग की परिस्थिति या अध्ययन पर निर्भर करते हैं।

rows.before: गलत जगह DNA के लिए कोशिका का अलार्म। विकिरण, कीमोथेरेपी और ADC DNA को कोशिकाद्रव्य में बहाते हैं; cGAS इसे पकड़ता है, STING अलार्म बजाता है और इंटरफ़ेरॉन प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र को बुलाता है।
rows.after: cGAS DNA को पहचानने वाला सेंसर है, जो STING के ज़रिए संकेत प्रक्रिया को सक्रिय कर सकता है। मापा गया संकेत और प्रतिरक्षा पर प्रभाव कोशिका और परिस्थिति पर निर्भर करते हैं।

rows.before: cGAS-STINGは、DNAが本来あるべきでない場所にあることを知らせる細胞の警報装置である。放射線、化学療法、ADCはDNAを細胞質にこぼれ出させる。cGASがそれを検知し、STINGが警報を鳴らし、インターフェロンが免疫系を呼び寄せる。
rows.after: cGASは、STINGを介したシグナル伝達を活性化しうるDNAセンサーです。測定されるシグナルや免疫への影響は、細胞や状況によって異なります。

rows.before: それ以外は効いている分子標的療法の中で、1つか2つの病変だけが増大する状態である。その病変を治療し、経口薬は継続する。
rows.after: オリゴ増悪は、治療中に他の病変が抑えられている一方で、限られた病変が進行する状態です。定義や局所治療を加える根拠は、臨床状況や研究によって異なります。

rows.before: Quando só um ou dois pontos crescem em uma terapia-alvo que ainda funciona; trate os pontos e mantenha o comprimido.
rows.after: Na oligoprogressão, um conjunto limitado de lesões progride enquanto o restante da doença permanece controlado durante o tratamento. A definição e as evidências para acrescentar tratamento local dependem do contexto clínico ou do estudo.

rows.before: O alarme da célula para DNA no lugar errado. Radiação, quimioterapia e ADCs derramam DNA no citoplasma; cGAS detecta, STING dispara o alarme e o interferon chama o sistema imune.
rows.after: cGAS é um sensor de DNA que pode ativar a sinalização por STING. O sinal medido e o efeito imunológico dependem da célula e do contexto.

rows.before: 在其他方面仍有效的靶向治疗中仅一两个病灶生长；处理病灶并继续用药。
rows.after: 寡进展是指治疗期间，其他病灶仍受控制，但有限的部分病灶出现进展。其定义以及增加局部治疗的证据取决于具体临床情境或研究。

rows.before: 细胞对错位DNA的警报。放疗、化疗和ADC把DNA洒入胞质；cGAS探测到，STING拉响警报，干扰素召来免疫系统。
rows.after: cGAS是DNA感受器，可以激活经STING传递的信号。测得的信号和免疫效应取决于细胞和具体情境。

rows.before: 线性二次模型：放疗用来比较不同分割方案的公式——细胞杀伤由与剂量成正比和与剂量平方成正比的两部分组成，二者之比（α/β）反映组织对单次剂量大小的敏感程度。
rows.after: 线性二次模型将与剂量成正比的项和与剂量平方成正比的项结合起来描述放射反应。其应用取决于组织、评价终点及照射方式。

rows.before: 生物等效剂量（BED）与EQD2：把任何放疗方案换算成统一“货币”，从而比较例如五次大剂量与25次小剂量的方法；EQD2以等效的2 Gy分次总剂量表达同一含义。
rows.after: 生物有效剂量（BED）在给定模型和组织参数假设下比较照射方式，不能据此确定临床结局或安全性相同。EQD2是在同一模型假设下换算为每次2 Gy的等效总剂量。

rows.before: When only one or two spots grow while a pill is otherwise still working; treat the spots and keep the pill.
rows.after: A few lesions grow while other cancer stays controlled during treatment. That pattern alone does not decide whether adding local treatment helps or which medicine to continue.

rows.before: The cell's alarm for DNA in the wrong place. When it goes off, the immune system is called in.
rows.after: cGAS senses DNA and can switch on signals through STING. What is measured and how the immune system responds depend on the cell and the situation.

rows.before: The linear-quadratic model is the equation radiotherapy uses to compare schedules, with the alpha over beta ratio telling how much a tissue cares about the size of each dose.
rows.after: A radiation model includes a part proportional to dose and a part proportional to dose squared. Its use depends on the tissue, the outcome being studied and how radiation is delivered.

rows.before: Biologically effective dose is a way of turning any radiotherapy schedule into a common currency, so a few big doses can be fairly compared with many small ones.
rows.after: Biologically effective dose compares radiation patterns using a model and assumptions about the tissue. Equal calculated values do not prove equal treatment benefit or safety.
